reasoning: The skill already covers many cache and schema rules, so the merged edits focus on actionable clarifications not already stated. The call-planning checklist and result-binding rule reinforce the optimizer’s preferred workflow. For hotel dates, the patches conflict on whether itinerary or flight dates can supply stay dates; the merged rule keeps the skill’s explicit prohibition on borrowing flight dates, while allowing checkout to be calculated from an explicitly stated stay length. The party-size and optional-field guidance is combined into one edit because it targets the same paragraph. No edits target the protected section.

edits.target: - Before emitting code, audit the planned calls against the latest turn and full conversation: for each new request or accepted preference, identify its intended item, domain, relation, and schema-supported argument, then verify that a planned call includes it. Do not reprocess unchanged domains. Use only a listed, compatible cache result for refinement; if none exists and mandatory inputs are available, search instead of filtering. After the audit, use `print("No planning needed")` only if no requested action or constraint remains unsatisfied by valid cached results.
edits.content: - Before emitting code, make a short call plan by diffing the latest user turn against the full conversation and listed cache entries. List each still-pending action separately by domain and location, and each explicitly stated flight leg, including a reversed return leg. For each, identify only the newly introduced constraints, the compatible listed cache result (if any), and whether mandatory inputs are available; choose direct cache reuse, refinement from that result, a new search, or a request for missing inputs. Include every ready action even if another is blocked, skip unchanged domains, and verify that every planned action has its required call or valid cache disposition. Use `print("No planning needed")` only when no requested action or constraint remains unsatisfied by valid cached results.

edits.target: Before searching, match each required tool field to an explicit value in the full conversation; related context does not automatically satisfy that field. For example, a reunion date is not necessarily a flight departure date, and restaurant cuisine or budget does not supply the required restaurant city. Do not infer missing mandatory values or use defaults. Assess readiness independently for each requested domain and, where applicable, each city or leg: proceed with searches or refinements for domains whose required inputs are available even if another is blocked. Make one `seek_information` call asking only for all missing mandatory inputs across blocked domains. Hotel check-in and check-out dates must be explicit; do not borrow them from flight dates or infer a neighborhood. Optional preferences are not mandatory inputs.

Assess readiness independently for each requested domain and, where applicable, each city or leg: proceed with searches or refinements for domains whose required inputs are available even if another is blocked. Make one `seek_information` call asking only for all missing mandatory inputs across blocked domains. Hotel check-in must be explicit. If the user explicitly states the stay length in nights, calculate checkout with `adjust_date(date=checkin_date, delta_days=nights)`; otherwise checkout must be explicit. Do not borrow hotel dates from flight dates or infer a neighborhood. Optional preferences are not mandatory inputs.

edits.target: - Carry forward relevant details from the conversation and include explicitly supplied criteria in the appropriate call. Send only schema-supported parameters; do not infer amenities, ratings, or other preferences. Do not infer exact party or room counts from broad descriptions such as “family.” Treat “solo” as one traveler only when a supported traveler-count field is available; do not infer a room count from it. A traveler count is not a flight-search parameter unless the schema provides one.
edits.content: - Carry forward relevant details from the conversation and include explicitly supplied criteria in the appropriate call. Send only schema-supported parameters; do not infer amenities, ratings, or other preferences. Omit optional fields the user did not state rather than setting them to `False`. Keep each constraint attached to its stated domain; for example, a flight budget is not a hotel budget. Do not infer exact party or room counts from broad descriptions such as “family.” Treat “solo” as one traveler only when a supported traveler-count field is available; do not infer a room count from it. Map an explicitly stated number of hotel travelers to `num_people` when the schema supports it; if added in a later turn, refine the latest compatible hotel result using only this new constraint. A traveler count is not a flight-search parameter unless the schema provides one.

edits.target: - Bind the exact return value of every search, filter, sort, and nearest-results call to a variable, then save it with `save_to_cache` under a unique, descriptive key. Save refined results under a new key. Do not substitute hand-built dictionaries or redefined models for tool result objects.
edits.content: - A tool call is incomplete until its exact returned object is bound to a variable and saved with `save_to_cache` under a unique, descriptive key. In the code, bind then save every search, filter, sort, and nearest-results call; save each leg and each refinement separately under a new key. Never emit a bare call or substitute hand-built dictionaries or redefined models for tool result objects.

edits.target: - Treat each explicitly described flight segment as its own search, using that leg’s origin, destination, and departure date. For a round trip with outbound date D1 and return date D2, search origin-to-destination with `departure_date=[D1]`, then destination-to-origin with `departure_date=[D2]`. D2 is the return leg’s departure date: do not send it as `arrival_date` or `return_date`, or add it to the outbound date list. Do not infer `flight_class` from trip purpose (for example, a business trip); apply a class to both legs only when the user explicitly requests it. Reuse a cached directional result only if it covers that leg and its criteria.
edits.content:
- “One-way” describes the requested travel direction, not the number of stops. Do not infer nonstop service or set `num_layovers=[0]` unless the user explicitly requests no stops.
- Translate flight time wording into the schema’s accepted time-range format. For “by T” or “no later than T,” use the earliest valid time as the lower endpoint and T as the upper endpoint; when the user also says “as early as possible,” use the start of the day as the lower endpoint. Apply departure and arrival time constraints to their respective fields, and do not invent seconds-based values or other unsupported formats.

edits.target: ## Validate tool arguments and preserve user intent
edits.content: - The tools listed in the prompt are already defined in the execution environment. Call them directly; do not import tool modules or redefine tools or their models.

edits.target: - Validate value encoding as well as argument names. For fields documented as lower/upper endpoint lists, represent an exact requested value x as `[x, x]`; do not pass a scalar or singleton list, widen the value, or treat it as a minimum. Follow the schema for non-exact bounds and do not invent endpoints.
edits.content: - For a schema field that represents a maximum nightly hotel budget, map wording such as “around N per night” to `budget=N` unless the user explicitly gives a range or tolerance.

edits.target: - Disambiguate closely related amenity fields using the tool’s phrase-to-field semantics rather than casual synonym matching. When a hotel schema exposes both fields, map “fitness center” to `has_fitness_class` and a literal request for a “gym” to `gym_present`.
edits.content: - When the restaurant schema has no dedicated nightshade-allergy field but exposes `has_tomato_allergy_options`, map a nightshade-allergy accommodation request to that field; do not substitute an unrelated allergy option such as nut-allergy options.

edits.target: - Interest in visiting or dining at a place alone does not imply a proximity request or require a nearest-results call.
edits.content: - This no-nearest rule does not cancel an attraction request: when the user wants to visit a named attraction, retrieve a compatible result for that exact name or search with `attraction_name`; include an explicitly stated attraction `type` as well. A generic or category-only attraction result does not cover a separately named site.

edits.target: - Pass the relevant result objects for the two domains being compared. Set `groupBy` to the domain whose candidates the user wants ranked or recommended (the focal domain), not the reference domain: hotels near an attraction use `groupBy="hotel"`, while restaurants near a hotel use `groupBy="restaurant"`.
edits.content: - For an explicit request for hotels or restaurants near a named attraction, treat “near” as a cross-domain relation: do not pass the attraction name as a hotel or restaurant `neighborhood`. Ensure the exact attraction result is available, then call `search_nearest` with the relevant results and the requested focal domain.
